text: 🇲🇽🎓 Sheinbaum doubled the goal: 400,000 new high school places so no teenager is left out. "We will have 400,000 new places, because the best place for teenagers to be is in school. The President doubled the goal — we had planned 200,000 places, and she told us we must make it 400,000." — Tania Rodríguez, Undersecretary of Upper Secondary Education In 2025, 88 schools were built or expanded (44,000 places). In 2026: 485 more schools, 156,240 places, over 10 billion pesos. Enrollment for the new Bachillerato Nacional "Margarita Maza" is open.

🇲🇽⚖️ A US court ruled Meta legally responsible for the harm its platform design causes children — and ordered the design changed. "The problem is not bad users posting negative content; it is a system designed to foster overuse, unwanted contact, and exposure to unwanted, harmful content." — Dr. Ravi Iyer, USC Neely Center, on the New Mexico v. Meta ruling The New Mexico ruling is the first to force a platform to modify design decisions: age verification, hidden like counts for minors, no push notifications at night or school hours, usage time caps, and private-by-default teen accounts — for 5 years.

🇲🇽📱 Meta's own internal research: 13% of Instagram users aged 13-15 received unwanted sexual advances in a single week. "Meta's own internal research revealed that 13% of Instagram users between 13 and 15 years old had received some unwanted sexual advance in the last 7 days." — Dr. Ravi Iyer, former Meta data-science research lead, at Mexico's morning press conference The figure comes from Meta's internal research made public in the New Mexico v. Meta litigation. A related internal survey found 19.2% of children 13-15 saw unwanted nudity or sexual content in one week. Iyer, now at USC's Neely Center, spent 4.5 years at Meta designing social networks.

🇲🇽⛽ 90% of Mexico's gas stations sell regular gasoline under 24 pesos — average 23.68. The voluntary price agreement is up for renewal. "The national average price of regular gasoline is 23.68 pesos. That is 11,725 stations, around 90% of them, selling regular gasoline under 24 pesos." — Iván Escalante, Federal Consumer Prosecutor (Profeco) 86% of stations sell diesel under 27 pesos. Profeco named a BP in Puebla selling diesel at 29.99 with a 3.94-peso margin — stations "still flying over the fence with prices."

🇲🇽💵 State-owned Finabien marks one year as the remittance service that pays the most for migrants' dollars. "Finabien marks one year as the remittance provider that pays the most for the dollars our countrymen send, in the account-deposit or transfer mode." — Iván Escalante, Federal Consumer Prosecutor (Profeco) On a $400 transfer, Finabien pays 6,987.38 pesos; the worst performer, Ria Money Transfer, pays 6,559.17 — a 428-peso gap per transfer. Profeco monitors around 15 remittance services weekly.

text: 🇲🇽📱 16 Mexican states already regulate cellphones in schools. The goal is nationwide — but teachers get asked first. "16 states of the Republic already regulate it, and the goal is to regulate it across the whole country. But first we are going to ask the teachers: what is your opinion?" — President Claudia Sheinbaum Sheinbaum cited US court rulings that found social media platforms harm children's mental and physical health. After the school-council debate, Mexico will discuss wider regulation of addictive platform design.

text: 🇲🇽📱 More than one million teachers in 200,000 schools will debate what to do about cellphones in classrooms. "More than one million teachers in more than 200,000 schools across all states will participate. We want teachers to propose and debate what must be done about the presence of digital devices in schools." — Mario Delgado, Secretary of Public Education The debate happens August 24-25 during the Consejo Técnico Intensivo, the week teachers prepare the new school year. A regional forum with experts opens Wednesday in Monterrey.

🇲🇽💻 <u>MEXICO'S TECH ENGINE: COMPUTER EXPORTS UP 178%, DRIVING THE EXPORT BOOM</u>

Mexico's exports of data-processing machines surged 177.57% from January to May — 76.75 of every 100 additional export dollars came from this sector alone, per a Banco BASE analysis of Banxico and Inegi figures reported by El Economista. Servers and processing units shipped to the US hit 60.4 billion dollars in the first half, against 80.5 billion in all of 2025. Total exports reached a record 389.7 billion dollars, up 24.62%, with Chihuahua and Jalisco leading the AI-hardware corridors. The AI revolution runs on hardware assembled in Mexico.
